title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_ancients 
 age_of_ancients : Long ago, the world was an unformed, homogeneous place which lacked a true concept of disparity. The grey, rocky land was perpetually shrouded in fog, and the landscape was dominated by towering stone archtrees which extended into endless clouds. The everlasting dragons, ancient and immortal entities who transcended the later concepts of life and death, were the dominant beings. This period was known as the Age of Ancients.

Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_age_of_ancients 
 the_age_of_ancients : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

Before the Age of Fire was the Age of Ancients. It was a time in which the world was colorless and shrouded by fog. The land consisted of gray crags, archtrees and Everlasting Dragons, who were the rulers of the world. Humans and other creatures had yet to make an impression upon the world.

title: Age of Ancients
snippet:
Age of Ancients -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Ancients the world was undistinguished and covered in fog: a land of gray rocks, great trees and everlasting dragons; everything was the same and time didn't exist.But at some point the First Flame appeared and brought "disparity" into the world, allowing the existence of everything and its opposite: heat and cold, life and death, light and dark.

It was during this time that the Lord Souls were found near the Flame. The three Lords who found them (Nito, Gwyn and the Witch of Izalith) formed a coalition and used the power of their newly discovered souls to challenge the Dragons, starting a very long and destructive war. However, there was a fourth Lord Soul, the Dark Soul, which was found by the Furtive Pygmy. The only known act via this Lord was the fragmentation of their soul becoming the birth of Humanity, who would fight side by side with the Lords.

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_fire 
 age_of_fire : With the dragons defeated, the Lords took over the world, ruling as Gods from their seat of power in the land of Lordran. It was a prosperous era, and many nations were born. In time, however, the First Flame began to fade, and with it the power of the Gods, leading to an era of decay and the emergence of the Undead Curse. If the Flame were to gutter out completely, it would end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Age of Fire -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

title: Age of Dark
snippet:
Age of Dark -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Age of Dark begins when the First Flame fades completely, thus ending the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods that gained their power from it.
Since the Flame continues to burn until it goes out naturally, the Dark Age should have arrived, as naturally, when it had exhausted its fuel.

Despite the Age of Dark being a ubiquitous concept throughout the *Dark Souls* series, it is never the "current" state of the world in any of the existing games. Each of the *Dark Souls* games takes place during a late point in the Age of Fire, a point which could theoretically lead to the beginning of the Age of Dark, but which does not do so during the normal course of gameplay, with one possible exception.

However, it is not necessarily an existence completely devoid of fire and illumination as it might seem, as the Dark Soul of humanity itself is capable of producing everlasting flames, even if cold and generating light sources.

Originally, it had been expected that the Age of Fire would be followed by an Age of Dark. However, following mankind's oppression under the Darksign since time immemorial, fanned by the unnatural prolongation of the First Flame's life, the Dark Soul and its fragments have been corrupted and stagnated. Among these byproducts of the Age of Fire are dregs, the decayed sedimentation of humanity; as well as ferocious pus which break out whenever the link of fire is threatened. These heavy, raucous outgrowths were evidence of that which lay beyond natural darkness.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: What exactly the term "Age of Dark" implies is never made explicitly clear in the games, however it is stated in the canonical *Dark Souls Trilogy Compendium* to be a time when the Light fades, a Dark Lord is heralded, and humanity dominates the world. When the protagonists are given information about the Age of Dark, it typically comes from the mouths of potentially unreliable narrators, of whom Kaathe and his counterpart, Kingseeker Frampt, are examples. Kaathe asserts that the Age of Dark is "the age of men," presumably meaning the Age of those possessing Humanity in contrast to the Age of the Gods, and also declares that Gwyn "resisted the course of nature" when he linked the Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Through another questline, the player can cooperate with Yuria, a leader of the Sable Church of Londor, who urges the Ashen One to take the Flame for themselves, to usher in an Age of Dark; for the Sisters of the Sable Church were under the guidance of Kaathe. This is Ending 4: "The Usurpation of Fire", where the Flame is wrested by the Ashen One, who is to lead the Age of Man as the Lord of Hollows. By the time of *Dark Souls III*, the undead curse has been accepted by the people of Londor, who have come to view it as a blessing, and their Hollow form as the "true face of man".

title: Age of Dark
snippet: According to Darkstalker Kaathe, the Chosen Undead, protagonist of *Dark Souls*, is destined to bring about the Age of Dark, as they are the descendant of the Furtive Pygmy, who possessed the Dark Soul and divided it among early humans in the form of Humanity. Should the Chosen Undead abandon the First Flame to die out after the defeat of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, they will "usher in the Age of Dark", and become the fabled "Dark Lord" of whom Kaathe speaks. It is important to note that Kaathe tells the Chosen Undead that the Age of Dark had apparently already begun shortly before Gwyn chose to link the Flame, though it was seemingly ended and replaced by the Age of Fire when the Flame was linked.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. title: Lore
snippet:
Lore -  Dark Souls - storyline - the_first_flame 
 the_first_flame : The advent of fire occurred, and with it came heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. The First Flame was born, source of all fire. However, from the dark came humanoid creatures - Hollows. These creatures found the Lord Souls near the flames and took on the powers they gave. They were:
Gravelord Nito, The First of the Dead, who offered much of his own soul to death, granting him the ability to administer the death of all life.
The Witch of Izalith, who became the leader of the flame sorcerers, later the so-called "Daughters of Chaos".
Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, who was to achieve great things in his life.
A fourth unique Lord Soul called the "Dark Soul" was found by the Furtive Pygmy, who is the ancestor of the humans. They are supposed to bring about the Age of Dark, in which humanity rules the world. A distant descendant of him is the Chosen Undead.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - ending 
 ending : Fulfilling the purpose for which they were brought back to life, the Ashen One links the First Flame and becomes a Lord of Cinder. The Flame connects with their body, slowly setting them ablaze as they sit beside the bonfire.

Although in theory, this leads to a continuation of the once-glorious Age of Fire, this linking of the Flame is but a shadow of the linking as can be performed by the Chosen Undead in *Dark Souls*, echoing the significant weakening of the First Flame, which instead of engulfing the Kiln into an explosive blaze of fire remains weak, barely kindled anew. The world remains dim and covered in ash, with the sun still obscured by a fire-dripping eclipse that resembles the Darksign, further exemplifying that this prolonged Age of Fire will pale when compared to days of old.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". In doing so, the Ashen One would inherit what little lifeforce remains of the First Flame, and thus become a worthy Lord of Men—that is, a "Lord of Hollows", as it has come to be referred to. title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Dark Lord
snippet:
Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: Sunlight Spear (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Sunlight Spear (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - description 
 description : Miracle of Gwyn, the First Lord.
Hurls a sunlight spear.

The tales of Gwyn's Archdragon hunts describe the inception of the Age of Fire.

title: Darksign
snippet:
Darksign -  Dark Souls II - item - lore 
 lore : Gwyn had foreseen the Age of Dark at the end of the Age of Fire and, fearing the infinite potential of the Dark Soul that the Furtive Pygmy found and the Humanity that inherited it, he forced a ring of fire around the Dark Soul to contain its powers and making every new human assume a weakened form and bear the Darksign. In addition, various groups were created to encourage worshipping Gwyn and his kin as Gods, such as the Way of White, the oldest and most powerful cultural organization centered around the veneration of the gods of Anor Londo, who spread Miracles to humans and cultivated the cult of the Age of Fire and the linking of the Flame.

title: Liliane
snippet: Liliane is a founding mentor of the Sable Church, and the youngest sister to Elfriede and Yuria. The three sisters at one point entered into the service of the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, becoming his maidens. The Primordial Serpent taught them his art of the Dark Hand, which could sap the essence of its victims. The sisters pursued Kaathe's goal of ending the Age of Fire founded by the gods and ushering the Age of Dark, and searched for a Dark Lord whom they would empower to usurp the First Flame and use its powers to lead humans into a new age. To this end, the three sisters used their battle prowess to establish the Sable Church, an organization that claimed to offer salvation to Hollows. The Church became a haven for those with unsavory or blurry pasts, along with other rejects of the Age of Fire. An increasing number of Undead and Hollows flocked to the Church, forming a society of wretchedly aged, deceitful, deeply detested Hollows. Their realm would be known as Londor, where

title: The Deep
snippet:
It is unclear what would have become of Aldrich at the end of the Age of Fire. While the champion of the Deep has already been defeated when the Ashen One visits the Ringed City or the Dreg Heap, it seems that his visions of an incoming Age of Deep Sea were close to coming to pass, with the remnants of the world of Man bustling with the sunken, stagnated dregs of humanity, the malformed legacy of the Dark Soul which had been suppressed by the Darksign for millennia.

To prevent the advent of the Age of Deep following the weakening of the First Flame, the plan of the Sable Church of Londor has become to tear the Flame off its Kiln and preserve it within a Lord of Hollows who can exploit its power, freezing the state of the world thanks to their Dark Sigil.

title: Souls of Lords
snippet:
Souls of Lords -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Soul of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

Lord Gwyn bequeathed most of his power to the Gods, and burned as cinder for the First Flame, but even so, Lord Gwyn's soul is a powerful thing indeed.

Soul of the Bed of Chaos and the mother of all demons. This Lord Soul was found at the dawn of the Age of Fire.

The Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame from a soul, but instead created a distorted being of chaos and fire. Its power formed a bed of life which would become the source of all demons, and is more than enough to satiate the Lordvessel.

Soul of Gravelord Nito, first of the dead. This Lord Soul was discovered at the dawn of the Age of Fire.

Gravelord Nito administers the death of all manner of beings. The power of his soul is so great that it satiates the Lordvessel, despite the fact that much of its energy has already been offered to death.

title: Courland
snippet: At a certain point the First Flame began to fade again and the first Fire Keeper of Lothric had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a "barren plane of endless darkness". For this reason, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition, was called to become a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Defying his frail appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Champion, something for which he himself expresses remorse and asks to be forgiven. Despite his role, Ludleth was then exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric, ensuring that the first Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes and that all future maidens like her were deprived of their sight, to prevent them from observing the future without the light of the First Flame. title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
Chosen Undead -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : The title of "Chosen Undead" is a reference to a prophecy concerning the end of the Age of Fire. It states that at the very end of the Age of Fire, an undead champion will appear and undertake the pilgrimage to ring the Bells of Awakening in "the Land of Ancient Lords," Lordran.

The Chosen Undead is a human, and thus, a descendant of the Furtive Pygmy, one of the original Lords who claimed the Dark Soul.

title: Chaos (mechanic)
snippet:
Chaos (mechanic) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Ancients, the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great and powerful firestorms. At the time, the Witch and her followers were powerful flame sorcerers who lived in the city of Izalith. Blacksmiths of the ancient city crafted powerful weapons using Chaos arts. Thus, during the earliest known ages of the world, Chaos developed its reputation as a powerful force.

Eventually, the Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame. What she instead produced was a twisted being of chaotic fire: the Bed of Chaos, source of all demons. Several of the Witch's daughters were transformed into chaos demons, and her son became the monstrous Ceaseless Discharge.

title: Darkstalker Kaathe
snippet:
Darkstalker Kaathe -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Darkstalker Kaathe greets the Chosen Undead and tells his side of the story: that the player is not to renew the Age of Fire by rekindling the First Flame, but is in fact the descendant of the one who possessed the "Dark Soul", and shall be responsible for bringing about the Age of Dark. Kaathe will transport the player to Firelink Altar in order to place the Lordvessel, and then instructs the player to collect the other Lord Souls in order to confront Gwyn, Lord of Cinder.

Kaathe can initiate players into the Darkwraith covenant.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet:
Primordial Serpents -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations!**

There are two named Primordial Serpents in the game: Kingseeker Frampt and Darkstalker Kaathe. Frampt was a friend of Lord Gwyn and is possibly working with Gwyndolin, as Gwyndolin created the illusion of Gwynevere, who beseeches the Chosen Undead listen to Frampt and link the First Flame. Kaathe, conversely, wishes for the Chosen Undead to bring forth an Age of Dark—also referred to as the Age of Man—by leaving the First Flame to die out, and becoming the Dark Lord of mankind.

title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - age_of_ancients 
 age_of_ancients : The Humans were created by the Furtive Pygmy, a forgotten Lord from the dawn of Fire, who claimed a small spark known as the Dark Soul. With this soul, the Pygmy raised up the Human race, binding their nature with the Dark. When the other Lords prepared to battle the Dragons, they came to the Humans, and conscripted them into their ranks. To this end, Humans began to forge arms and armor in the Abyss, which drew upon the power of a dark flame. Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, and his children, the Gods, cast a seal of fire upon them due to their perilous nature. So it was that the Human army, who were dubbed the Ringed Knights, set out with the Lords and their armies to eradicate the Everlasting Dragons, but due to their disruptive potential, their roles went unrecorded in histories.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Nameless King is the firstborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. He was worshipped by humans as the "god of war".

title: Dragon Memories
snippet:
Dragon Memories -  Dark Souls II - location - trivia 
 trivia : The dragon memory seems to be located after the War with the Dragons during the Age of Ancients from *Dark Souls*.
This is one of the few areas of the game that has its own atmospheric soundtrack.
Dropping anything in Majula will cause it to appear in the sky of this area.

title: Undead
snippet:
Undead -  Dark Souls - mechanic - causes 
 causes : The curse of undeath was created when Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and Ruler of the Age of Fire, began to feel threatened by the descendants of the Furtive Pygmy: humans were immortal beings, born from the Dark yet able to live in a world enlightened by the Fire, whose souls did not lose power despite being endlessly split and multiplied. According to the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, the gods were intimidated by this unexplored potential of the Dark Soul. They had briefly glimpsed at the smidgen of life emanated from the primordial human knights, and feared the eventual overthrow of Anor Londo and its Age of Fire. Therefore, a complex and ingenious apparatus was set in motion with the goal to mould humanity into a subservient, weak people that would not only serve the Age of Fire, but also refused to relinquish it to make way for the Age of Dark.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
None of them will slow down when in the water at the bottom of the arena, unlike the player character.
Even at lower levels of NG+, this boss fight becomes one of the most challenging ones in the game, as the three enemies can all kill the player in only a few hits. In addition to that, the player cannot attack the same enemy for more than a few hits without them rolling away, especially when they have no means of stunlocking them or dealing consistent damage through ripostes or backstabs, making this fight incredibly tough. All of this makes summoning other players or NPC phantoms a very good idea.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : There is no actual lore associated to the characters, although given one's title as "Graverobber", they may have come to Shulva in search of its many treasures. Whether they are still sentient, or have turned Hollow, is unclear. The Graverobber is female, while the other two are male.

Ancient Soldier Varg dons Havel the Rock's equipment: as his name implies he is very old, he might have been an actual member of Havel's knighthood. Meanwhile, Cerah dons Lucatiel's Mask; it is likely not Lucatiel's actual headwear, and rather one belonging to another knight of Mirrah.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - summoning 
 summoning : Rapacious Andrei and Ruined Aflis are available for summoning as soon as the player enters the Cave of the Dead.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : All three enemies are actually Hollow underneath their armor.
The Afflicted Graverobber is female, and uses the hollowed female voice when hit or staggered.
It's possible that Varg was one of Havel's Warriors, owed to his ownership of their equipment as well as his title of "Ancient Soldier", implying he belongs to an older era than that of Drangleic.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - description 
 description : A group of three NPCs composed of a tanky warrior with high defense and damage output, a more dextrous powerstancing enemy that can easily prock bleed during the encounter, and an archer that prefers to stay at the back and harrass with his great arrows, but who can also switch to a melee weapon when forced into one-on-one combat.

The unnamed "Afflicted Graverobber" dons the Alva Set and wields one Berserker Blade in each hand.

Ancient Solder Varg uses equipment associated with Havel the Rock: Havel's Set, the Dragon Tooth, and Havel's Greatshield.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : It doesn't matter in which order the three are killed, the drops at the end of the fight will be the same.
As a phantom, it is possible to get a Puzzling Stone Sword, Lightning Clutch Ring, Promised Walk of Peace, Dried Root, or a Sanctum Mace as a reward for completing this fight in another world, allowing players who do not own the DLC to use these items too.
Varg has 7 Estus Flasks total. Coupled with his incredible defense, it makes him the most durable foe of the encounter.
None of them will slow down when in the water at the bottom of the arena, unlike the player character.

title: Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer
snippet:
Afflicted Graverobber, Ancient Soldier Varg, and Cerah the Old Explorer -  Dark Souls II - boss - location 
 location : They are found at the end of the Cave of the Dead.
